about: The shop decorating plan, edited with `npm run style`. Questions are added here; answers come back from the page.

paints.name: Purple
paints.note: The paint every shelf has today.

paints.name: Crimson
paints.note: For example: a reward for a 5-star review streak.

paints.text: How should a player get a new paint? For example: buy it from a supplier, get it free at a shop level, or earn it as a reward. It can be a mix of these; say which paints come which way.
Once a player owns a paint, can they use it on as many shelves as they like, forever? Or does a can run out after a certain number of shelves, so they buy more?
Should repainting a shelf cost money or take time (like stocking does), or be instant and free once you own the paint?
Where does the player go to paint something? For example: a choice in each shelf's menu, a paint mode on the manager tablet, or something else.
Mixing your own paint: when should it unlock, what should it cost, and should mixed paints have any limits besides never being pitch black?

shelves.text: The strip along the top front edge of each shelf shows which way it faces. When you're moving a shelf, should the strip replace the blue box that shows where customers stand, or should both show?
Should the strip glow? If so, steady, slowly pulsing, or the player's choice per shelf?
Besides the shelf body and the strip, is there any other part of a shelf you'd want to color separately (for example the boards the items sit on, or the feet)?
Should other things in the shop be paintable too, like the register, the order terminal, the trash can, or decorations? Which ones?

room.text: Should a floor or wall color cover the whole shop at once, each room separately (sales floor, backroom), or single squares you paint one at a time?
Besides colors, do you want different floor and wall patterns to unlock, like metal grates, riveted plates, or hazard stripes?
Should decorating change anything in the game, like the Presentation score or what customers think, or is it purely for looks?

lighting.text: Should lights be things you buy and place like shelves, or built into the ceiling and walls so you only change their color and brightness?
Should the shop ever get dark enough that lights really matter (for example late shifts or a power cut), or is it always lit and lights are just for mood?
Should lighting affect customers or Presentation, for example dim corners selling less?
